Hook: When the old reaction is running before you notice it, Word Melt makes the invisible part of the pattern easier to catch.
Mission: Repeat the sound until the spell loses its language.
Game Move: Let Choose Charged begin the game. Let Return Seen end it.
How to Play:
🎮 WORD MELT // PLAY
One pass is enough. Follow what is written.

1. Choose Charged — Choose one charged word—not a whole painful story.
2. Say Gently — Say it gently and steadily for about twenty seconds.
3. Listen Moment — Listen for the moment it becomes rhythm, mouth movement, or noise.
4. Stop Room — Stop there and look around the room.
5. Return Seen — Meaning may return; you have seen it separate once.

⚡ EXIT — Finish Return Seen and leave the game there.
POWER-UP 1: Give yourself one second before Choose Charged: soften your jaw and unclench your hands.
POWER-UP 2: At Listen Moment, move your attention to one thing that is happening now.
POWER-UP 3: When you reach Return Seen, choose one action that fits the facts you found. Let this be the line you keep: Repeat the sound until the spell loses its language.
Win / Reward:
🏆 WIN SIGNAL
You notice the pull of the old pattern and can still choose Return Seen.

📸 MY RESULT
“I caught the pattern early enough to choose.”
Formula Flow: Choose Charged → Say Gently → Listen Moment → Stop Room → Return Seen
Safety:
PAUSE
Avoid this with slurs, trauma phrases, voices, or material that escalates symptoms.

POWER-UP 2: At Complete Version, separate responsibility from punishment.

Win / Reward:
🏆 WIN SIGNAL
You can do Challenge while some discomfort is still present.

📸 MY RESULT
“Something happened. It wasn't a definition of me.”
Formula Flow: Select Task → Increase → Complete Version → Challenge
Safety:
PAUSE

Hook: When the message in your head has become sharper than the facts, Set The Conversation Size makes the invisible part of the pattern easier to catch.
Mission: A conversation can be important and still need a smaller container today.
Game Move: Begin with Read Bandwidth. Move straight through to Set Reopen—no extra analysing.

🎮 SET THE CONVERSATION SIZE // PLAY
One pass is enough. Follow what is written.

1. Read Bandwidth — Choose your current safe bandwidth: ONE SENTENCE, THREE SENTENCES, or FULL CONVERSATION.
2. Choose Size — Name the purpose that must fit inside that size: acknowledge, request, pause, clarify, or repair.
3. Send Signal — Draft or say only the selected amount. Stop when the sentence limit is reached, even if more remains.
4. Set Reopen — Name when or under what condition the next level can reopen. If you cannot offer one, state that honestly without making a false promise.

POWER-UP 3: When you reach Set Reopen, choose one action that fits the facts you found. Let this be the line you keep: A conversation can be important and still need a smaller container today.

🏆 WIN SIGNAL
You notice the pull of the old pattern and can still choose Set Reopen.

📸 MY RESULT
“I separated what was said from what I added to it.”
Formula Flow: Read Bandwidth → Choose Size → Send Signal → Set Reopen
Safety:
PAUSE

Hook: Use Then / Now Subtitles when an old memory is being experienced like it is happening now. It turns the reaction into a small experiment.
Mission: Flashbacks need temporal translation.
Game Move: Start with Alternate Lines. When Date Location appears, the round is over.
How to Play:
🎮 THEN / NOW SUBTITLES // PLAY
Do the moves once and let the result be whatever it is.

1. Alternate Lines — When memory body alarm begins, alternate lines: THEN—state one past fact; NOW—state one current difference.
2. Include Age — Include age, place, available help, bodily freedom, and exits.
3. Keep Eyes — Keep eyes open and touch the environment after every pair.
4. Date Location — The screen may replay; the subtitles restore date and location.

⚡ END MOVE — Date Location. No second lap.
POWER-UP 1: Just before you start Alternate Lines, notice one sound in the room before continuing.
POWER-UP 2: At Keep Eyes, move your attention to one thing that is happening now.
POWER-UP 3: When you reach Date Location, choose one action that fits the facts you found. Take this line with you: Flashbacks need temporal translation.
Win / Reward:
🏆 WIN SIGNAL
At Date Location, you have at least one option the first reaction did not show you.

📸 MY RESULT
“That was then. I found something that is true now.”
Formula Flow: Alternate Lines → Include Age → Keep Eyes → Date Location
Safety:
PAUSE
Contact emergency or trauma support if sense of where you are does not return.

Hook: Enough Is A Current Fact catches the moment when your mind keeps circling without finding anything new and gives you another route.
Mission: Sufficiency can coexist with ambition.
Game Move: Move through the sequence once, from Identify Part to Choose Non.
How to Play:
🎮 ENOUGH IS A CURRENT FACT // PLAY
One short round. Nothing to solve beyond the moves.

1. Identify Part — Spot one part of the present condition that is genuinely adequate: shelter, breath, effort, support, knowledge, or time for the next step.
2. Receive Adequacy — Receive that adequacy without claiming everything is fine.
3. Choose Non — From this base, choose one non-desperate improvement.

⚡ FINISH — Choose Non closes the round.
POWER-UP 1: Before you begin Identify Part, let your shoulders drop and take one easy exhale.
POWER-UP 2: At Receive Adequacy, move your attention to one thing that is happening now.
POWER-UP 3: When you reach Choose Non, choose one action that fits the facts you found. If you remember one thing, make it this: Sufficiency can coexist with ambition.
Win / Reward:
🏆 WIN SIGNAL
You arrive at Choose Non with less need to obey the first answer.

📸 MY RESULT
“I stopped circling and found the next useful point.”
Formula Flow: Identify Part → Receive Adequacy → Choose Non
Safety:
PAUSE
Do not use contentment to minimise unmet needs or structural harm.

Ritual Title: CHANGE ONE THING, WATCH ONE FEELING
Hook: Change One Thing, Watch One Feeling is a tiny mind game for the moment when several feelings have merged into one heavy mass.
Mission: Two feelings untangle when one scene change moves only one of them.
Game Move: Touch Name Pair, follow the moves, and finish on Tag Driver.
How to Play:
🎮 CHANGE ONE THING, WATCH ONE FEELING // PLAY
Run the game exactly once, lightly.

1. Name Pair — Name two emotions in the mixture and rate each with a simple low, medium, or high—not a number.
2. Hold Scene — Hold the scene steady. Choose only one variable to test: person, time, place, audience, or outcome.
3. Swap Variable — Imagine that one variable changed for ten seconds. Keep every other fact the same.
4. Tag Driver — Notice which emotion moved and which stayed. Tag the changed variable as a likely driver, not a final explanation.

⚡ DONE — Complete Tag Driver, then return to your day.
POWER-UP 1: At the start of Name Pair, widen your gaze and notice the edges of the room.
POWER-UP 2: At Swap Variable, give the feeling a name without letting it make the decision.
POWER-UP 3: When you reach Tag Driver, choose one action that fits the facts you found. Keep only this lesson: Two feelings untangle when one scene change moves only one of them.
Win / Reward:
🏆 WIN SIGNAL
The old reaction loses a little speed before Tag Driver.

📸 MY RESULT
“The feeling wasn't one giant thing; it had parts.”
Formula Flow: Name Pair → Hold Scene → Swap Variable → Tag Driver
Safety:
PAUSE
Do not use imagined substitutions to rewrite trauma, deny facts, or continue once the scene becomes overwhelming or unreal.

Hook: When the old reaction is running before you notice it, Two Chairs, No Telepathy gives you something concrete to do with the moment.
Mission: Give both positions a voice without claiming either is fact.
Game Move: Start at Place Chairs. Stop at Dont And. Let the middle do the work.
How to Play:
🎮 TWO CHAIRS, NO TELEPATHY // PLAY
One clean round. Keep the moves simple.

1. Place Chairs — Place two chairs apart.
2. Speak Position — Speak from your position using first person.
3. Switch Chair — Move and answer as the other position, labelling imagination where knowledge is missing.
4. Dont And — Return to your chair and state what changed, what did not, and what real conversation may still be needed.

⚡ FINISH — Dont And closes the round.
POWER-UP 1: Before you begin Place Chairs, let your shoulders drop and take one easy exhale.
POWER-UP 2: At Switch Chair, move your attention to one thing that is happening now.
POWER-UP 3: When you reach Dont And, choose one action that fits the facts you found. Carry this rule with you: Give both positions a voice without claiming either is fact.
Win / Reward:
🏆 WIN SIGNAL
You can reach Dont And with more choice than you had at Place Chairs.

📸 MY RESULT
“I caught the pattern early enough to choose.”
Formula Flow: Place Chairs → Speak Position → Switch Chair → Dont And
Safety:
PAUSE
Avoid this alone for traumatic relationships or if role-switching feels disorganising.

Hook: When one moment is turning into a whole story, Tell It At The Speed Of Safety helps you test what your mind is telling you.
Mission: Disclosure should increase clarity, not steal control.
Game Move: Enter through Choose Trustworthy; leave as soon as you reach End Support. One pass is enough.
How to Play:
🎮 TELL IT AT THE SPEED OF SAFETY // PLAY
Play the moves, not the whole life story.

1. Choose Trustworthy — Choose a trustworthy listener and agree on time, confidentiality, and a stop signal.
2. Share — Share facts first, then feelings and meaning in tolerable detail.
3. Pause Orient — Pause to orient between sections.
4. End Support — End with what support you want now—not what the listener guesses.

⚡ DONE — Complete End Support, then return to your day.
POWER-UP 1: At the start of Choose Trustworthy, widen your gaze and notice the edges of the room.
POWER-UP 2: At Pause Orient, try the opposite possibility for ten seconds.
POWER-UP 3: When you reach End Support, choose one action that fits the facts you found. Keep the clean version: Disclosure should increase clarity, not steal control.
Win / Reward:
🏆 WIN SIGNAL
A small gap appears between the reaction and what you do at End Support.

📸 MY RESULT
“I caught the moment before it became the whole room.”
Formula Flow: Choose Trustworthy → Share → Pause Orient → End Support
Safety:
PAUSE
Stop when speech becomes flooding, detached, pressured, or unsafe.

Hook: If fear is making a possibility feel like a certainty, Make Fear Name A Deadline turns the mental noise into one playable move.
Mission: A warning must become testable before it can command you.
Game Move: One round only: enter at Pin Forecast, finish at Update Odds.
How to Play:
🎮 MAKE FEAR NAME A DEADLINE // PLAY
Play it once. No bonus analysis.

1. Pin Forecast — Rewrite the fear as one visible or audible forecast—not a vague catastrophe.
2. Set Clock — Give the forecast a real time window.
3. Score Odds — Set confidence from 0 to 100 before checking anything.
4. Observe Safely — Use only a naturally occurring safe observation; never manufacture a test.
5. Update Odds — Hold the result and update confidence in either direction.

⚡ LAST MOVE — Reach Update Odds and release the exercise.
POWER-UP 1: To open Pin Forecast, slow the next movement by about half.
POWER-UP 2: At Score Odds, look for the piece of evidence your first reaction ignored.
POWER-UP 3: When you reach Update Odds, choose one action that fits the facts you found. Use this as the exit rule: A warning must become testable before it can command you.
Win / Reward:
🏆 WIN SIGNAL
The pattern becomes easier to spot before you commit to Update Odds.

📸 MY RESULT
“Fear gave me certainty. Evidence gave me odds.”
Formula Flow: Pin Forecast → Set Clock → Score Odds → Observe Safely → Update Odds
Safety:
PAUSE
Do not test danger, invade privacy, or repeat the observation to chase certainty.

Hook: When your body alarm keeps turning itself up, Disassemble The Alarm Panel helps you test what your mind is telling you.
Mission: The whole alarm does not need to stop before one dial can move.
Game Move: Enter through Read Channels; leave as soon as you reach Check Panel. One pass is enough.
How to Play:
🎮 DISASSEMBLE THE ALARM PANEL // PLAY
Play the moves, not the whole life story.

1. Read Channels — Read three channels without searching your whole body: SPEED, PRESSURE, and TEMPERATURE. Use low, medium, or high.
2. Pick Smallest — Choose the safest channel with the lowest intensity. Do not pick the loudest one.
3. Move Dial — Move only that channel one step: slow one hand movement, soften one contact point, or adjust one safe layer of warmth or coolness.
4. Check Panel — Check whether that channel changed at all. Let the other two channels remain exactly as they are.

⚡ DONE — Complete Check Panel, then return to your day.
POWER-UP 1: At the start of Read Channels, widen your gaze and notice the edges of the room.
POWER-UP 2: At Move Dial, name the sensation in plain physical words—pressure, heat, tightness, movement.
POWER-UP 3: When you reach Check Panel, choose one action that fits the facts you found. Keep the clean version: The whole alarm does not need to stop before one dial can move.
Win / Reward:
🏆 WIN SIGNAL
A small gap appears between the reaction and what you do at Check Panel.

📸 MY RESULT
“My body sounded an alarm; I didn't have to turn it into danger.”
Formula Flow: Read Channels → Pick Smallest → Move Dial → Check Panel
Safety:
PAUSE
New, severe, or unusual physical symptoms require medical assessment. Stop for pain, faintness, breathing difficulty, confusion, or loss of orientation.

Hook: When one moment is turning into a whole story, Exist For One Minute Without Autobiography helps you test what your mind is telling you.

🎮 EXIST FOR ONE MINUTE WITHOUT AUTOBIOGRAPHY // PLAY
Play the moves, not the whole life story.

2. Stay Changing — Stay with changing sound, pressure, light, and movement.
3. Simple — Notice the simple ongoing sense of being present through those changes.

Win / Reward:
🏆 WIN SIGNAL
The first interpretation feels less final when you reach End Reclaim.

📸 MY RESULT
“I caught the moment before it became the whole room.”
Formula Flow: Dont Recall → Stay Changing → Simple → End Reclaim
Safety:
PAUSE
Stop if life-story quiet creates feeling unreal or detached from yourself.

Hook: Whose Handwriting Is On This Belief? works best when your mind has zoomed in so far that the rest disappeared. The goal is not to win an argument with your mind—just change the next move.
Mission: Inherited rules often feel like your own after the source fades.
Game Move: Let Name Modelled begin the game. Let Ask Whether end it.
How to Play:
🎮 WHOSE HANDWRITING IS ON THIS BELIEF? // PLAY
Stay with the sequence. You do not need to improve it.

1. Name Modelled — Name who modelled, rewarded, enforced, or normalised the belief.
2. Picture Original — Picture the original context and what compliance protected.
3. Ask Whether — Then ask whether current-you endorses it under present values and evidence.

⚡ EXIT — Finish Ask Whether and leave the game there.
POWER-UP 1: Give yourself one second before Name Modelled: soften your jaw and unclench your hands.
POWER-UP 2: At Picture Original, separate what you know from what you are predicting.
POWER-UP 3: When you reach Ask Whether, choose one action that fits the facts you found. Leave the exercise with this: Inherited rules often feel like your own after the source fades.
Win / Reward:
🏆 WIN SIGNAL
You can choose Ask Whether from what you noticed, not just from what you felt first.

📸 MY RESULT
“I put the missing context back into the picture.”
Formula Flow: Name Modelled → Picture Original → Ask Whether
Safety:
PAUSE
Avoid blaming cultures or individuals simplistically; systems transmit mixed messages.

Hook: When your mind has zoomed in so far that the rest disappeared, Move The Rule Between Worlds helps you test what your mind is telling you.
Mission: A rule must survive context before it earns the word universal.
Game Move: Enter through State Rule; leave as soon as you reach Keep Core. One pass is enough.

🎮 MOVE THE RULE BETWEEN WORLDS // PLAY
Play the moves, not the whole life story.

2. Change Context — Place it in three contrasting settings—for example family, workplace, and friendship—with different power and consequences.

4. Keep Core — Keep only the part that remains ethical and workable across contexts; Notice the rest as conditional.

Win / Reward:
🏆 WIN SIGNAL
A small gap appears between the reaction and what you do at Keep Core.

📸 MY RESULT
“I put the missing context back into the picture.”
Formula Flow: State Rule → Change Context → Compare Effects → Keep Core
